notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], robotis_ffw/scene_ffw_bg2.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. The scene includes robotis_ffw/ffw_bg2.xml. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge checks each of the 19 ctrl elements against the model's actuator_ctrlrange before writing data.ctrl, then mj_step runs ticks times. Every actuator is a <position> with inheritrange="1", so its interval is the driven joint's range (derived from the model at load time, not copied into a Limit). cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The card's other model scenes (the other FFW scenes, OMX, OMY, OP3, OpenMANIPULATOR-X and TurtleBot3) are not served: one package serves one device, and the driver and fake use models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the upstream is an XML model collection with no Python module, so the card's family-config/MujocoDriver decision is the right shape (no DEVIATION). MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (the form the SDK's own MujocoDriver tests use); the lock names it .fake:FakeMujoco. The stand-in parses the same scene and its include for the joint dimensions and per-actuator control ranges but integrates a placeholder first-order motion; it loads no mesh and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint, and the six gripper equality constraints are not applied.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; the model sets no <option timestep> (robotis_ffw/ffw_bg2.xml:4), the stand-in uses a 2 ms placeholder and the engine's default was not verified; there is no rendering; no physical FFW-BG2 robot is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware. The reference's timestep_ms 2 is that placeholder, not a claim about the engine.

WARNINGS (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND, because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the inputs the simulator family derives and that PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds six cases (model shape from the card scene, per-actuator control-range refusals and a valid control moving qpos, ticks advancing the model clock, reset, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. Install recon: the card has no install commands and the repository has no Python packaging; MuJoCo is needed only for the real-engine sim path, which was not run. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
